raised.value: $150M Series E in September 2026, bringing new funding raised this year to $650M and total funding to $1.02B at a $3.75B valuation

entry.idea: Ayar Labs replaces the electrical wiring between computer chips with light, letting AI data centers move far more data between chips while using less power.
entry.lesson: When physical wiring becomes the bottleneck holding back an entire industry's next leap in performance, deep hardware science aimed squarely at that bottleneck can attract huge strategic investment.
entry.name: Ayar Labs

growth.reason: It raised $650M in a single year, reached a $3.75B valuation, and secured direct strategic investment from AMD, Intel and NVIDIA, exceptionally strong momentum.

market.reason: Every AI data center provider worldwide faces the same chip-to-chip data bottleneck, a very large and urgent infrastructure market.

tech.reason: Building working optical interconnects that pack light-based data links right next to a chip is deep, years-in-the-making photonics hardware engineering, extremely hard to copy quickly.

entry.twist: Its optical connections sit right next to the chip itself (co-packaged optics), rather than as a separate add-on card, closing the distance that normally limits how fast chips can talk to each other.
entry.who_pays: Major chipmakers and AI infrastructure builders invest in and buy Ayar Labs' optical interconnect technology to build faster, more power-efficient AI hardware.
entry.why_now: AI data centers are hitting a wall where moving data between chips wastes more power and limits speed more than the chips' own computing, making a faster, lower-power connection method essential.

mentions.snippet: Optical interconnects for semiconductors; $150M more, $650M raised this year, moving to mass production.
